Overview

Audits That Add Value, Not Just Compliance

An audit shouldn't just be a statutory box to tick. Done properly, it surfaces control weaknesses, process gaps and reporting risks before they become bigger problems. We plan every audit around your actual business, not a generic checklist.

Our audit work is independent and evidence-based, with clear, actionable findings communicated directly to you or your board — not buried in jargon.

Types of Audit

Audit Services We Provide

📋

Statutory Audit

Independent audit of financial statements as required under the Companies Act for companies and other entities.

🔎

Internal Audit

Ongoing review of internal controls, processes and risk areas to strengthen governance between statutory audits.

🧾

Tax Audit

Audit under the Income Tax Act for businesses and professionals crossing the applicable turnover or receipts threshold.

📦

Stock Audit

Physical verification and valuation of inventory, commonly required by banks for working capital facilities.

🏢

Management Audit

Review of management processes, efficiency and decision-making systems to identify operational improvements.

Who Needs This

Audit Requirements Vary by Entity

  • Private and public companies requiring a statutory audit under the Companies Act
  • Businesses and professionals crossing the tax audit turnover threshold
  • Companies whose lenders require periodic stock audits
  • Growing businesses that want an internal audit function without hiring in-house
  • Boards seeking an independent review of management processes

Benefits

What a Proper Audit Gives You

  • Credible financial statements for lenders, investors and regulators
  • Early visibility into control weaknesses and process gaps
  • Reduced risk of penalties from non-compliance
  • Clear, documented findings — not vague observations

Our Process

How We Conduct an Audit

1. Planning

We understand your business, identify key risk areas, and agree the audit scope and timeline.

2. Fieldwork

Testing of transactions, controls and balances, with documented evidence at every step.

3. Findings Review

We walk you through observations and findings before the report is finalised — no surprises.

4. Reporting

A signed audit report is issued along with a management letter covering any recommendations.
